import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Komlós conjecture

The Komlós conjecture in discrepancy theory: there is a universal constant $K$ such
that for all $n, m$ and all vectors $v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with
$\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$, there exist signs $\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$$\left\|\sum\_{i=1}^n \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le K.$$

The best known bound is due to Banaszczyk, who proved that one can always achieve
$O(\sqrt{\log n})$. The Beck–Fiala theorem on the discrepancy of sparse set systems
is a special case (up to scaling), and the conjecture would imply the Beck–Fiala
conjecture that set systems of degree $t$ have discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrepancy_theory#Major_open_problems)
- [W. Banaszczyk, *Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies*,
  Random Structures & Algorithms **12** (1998), 351–360](https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1098-2418(199807)12:4%3C351::AID-RSA3%3E3.0.CO;2-S)
- [J. Spencer, *Six standard deviations suffice*,
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. **289** (1985), 679–706](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1985-0784009-0)
-/

namespace KomlosConjecture

/--
**The Komlós conjecture**

There exists a universal constant $K > 0$ such that for all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and
all vectors $v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$ (encoded here as
$\sum\_j v\_{ij}^2 \le 1$), there exist signs $\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left\|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le K$, i.e.
$\left|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_{ij}\right| \le K$ for every coordinate $j$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem komlos_conjecture :
    ∃ K : ℝ, 0 < K ∧ ∀ (n m : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ i, ∑ j, (v i j) ^ 2 ≤ 1) →
      ∃ ε : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
        ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ K := by
  sorry

/--
**Banaszczyk's theorem**

There exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for all $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and all vectors
$v\_1, \dots, v\_n \in \mathbb{R}^m$ with $\|v\_i\|\_2 \le 1$, there exist signs
$\varepsilon\_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ such that
$\left\|\sum\_i \varepsilon\_i v\_i\right\|\_\infty \le C \sqrt{\log(n + 2)}$.
This is the best known bound towards the Komlós conjecture. (The shift $n + 2$ inside
the logarithm is a harmless normalization keeping it positive for $n \in \{0, 1\}$.)

[W. Banaszczyk, *Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies*,
Random Structures & Algorithms **12** (1998), 351–360.]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem komlos_conjecture.variants.banaszczyk :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n m : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Fin m → ℝ),
      (∀ i, ∑ j, (v i j) ^ 2 ≤ 1) →
      ∃ ε : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
        ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ C * Real.sqrt (Real.log (n + 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: with no vectors at all ($n = 0$), the empty signed sum is $0$ in every
coordinate, so any constant bound holds.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem komlos_conjecture.variants.zero_vectors (m : ℕ) (v : Fin 0 → Fin m → ℝ) :
    ∃ ε : Fin 0 → ℝ, (∀ i, ε i = 1 ∨ ε i = -1) ∧
      ∀ j, |∑ i, ε i * v i j| ≤ 1 :=
  ⟨Fin.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, by simp⟩

end KomlosConjecture

findings.description: The module introduction (lines 28–30) calls the Beck–Fiala theorem a special case “up to scaling.” The standard incidence-matrix specialization instead gives the Beck–Fiala conjecture: scaling columns by t^(-1/2) turns the Komlós bound into K√t. Specializing the Banaszczyk variant gives O(√(t log n)), not the classical Beck–Fiala theorem’s 2t−1 bound. This is a background reference slip; the three Lean theorem statements are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: Bansal–Dadush–Garg, arXiv:1605.02882v3, §1 (intro.tex), distinguishes the proved 2t−1 theorem from the O(√t) conjecture, then calls Komlós a “substantial generalization of the Beck-Fiala conjecture” and explains the t^(-1/2) scaling. See also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beck%E2%80%93Fiala_theorem, Statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: “The Komlós conjecture would imply the Beck–Fiala conjecture that set systems of degree t have discrepancy O(√t), by scaling their incidence columns by t^(-1/2).”

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement expands the Euclidean unit-ball hypothesis into a sum of squares and the infinity-norm conclusion into simultaneous coordinate inequalities. It also permits empty families and zero-dimensional spaces.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real vectors, the squared Euclidean norm equals the sum of coordinate squares, so the hypothesis is exactly norm ≤ 1. For K ≥ 0, the infinity norm is ≤ K exactly when every coordinate has absolute value ≤ K, including zero-dimensional spaces. The real-valued sign function is explicitly constrained to ±1. Empty families have sum zero; zero-dimensional spaces impose no coordinate constraints. Review.norm_form_iff proves the full equivalence for all natural n and m in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source’s O(√log n) bound is expressed as a universal positive constant times √log(n+2), valid also at n=0 and n=1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 2, log n ≤ log(n+2) ≤ 2 log n, since n+2 ≤ n². Thus the bounds differ by at most a factor √2. The empty-family case has discrepancy zero, and a single admissible vector has discrepancy at most one, so enlarging the constant handles n=0,1 uniformly in m. Review.logarithmic_forms_iff proves the full equivalence with the unshifted formulation restricted to n ≥ 2. An eventual big-O bound also extends to all n ≥ 2 because the elementary discrepancy bound n handles any finite exceptional prefix uniformly in m.

sources_consulted: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, An Algorithm for Komlós Conjecture Matching Banaszczyk's bound, arXiv:1605.02882v3: abstract at https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02882 and LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1605.02882v3; especially §1 and the final paragraph of §4.

W. Banaszczyk, Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies (1998): abstract and bibliographic metadata read via https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1002/(sici)1098-2418(199807)12:4%3C351::aid-rsa3%3E3.0.co;2-s; bibliographic metadata also checked through Crossref.
J. Spencer, Six standard deviations suffice (1985): abstract and bibliographic metadata read via https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1985-0784009-0.
review.notes: No misformalization of the three Lean declarations was found. In particular, the Banaszczyk bound correctly depends on the number of vectors n, not necessarily the ambient dimension m: arXiv:1605.02882v3 explicitly states this bound and explains the reduction to polynomially many relevant coordinates. Wikipedia continues to list Komlós as open, and the solved/test tags agree with the checked sources and proof. The scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles with zero errors and warnings; it checks n=0, m=0, n=1, positivity of log(n+2), norm equivalences, and a concrete two-vector example. The equivalence proofs and the file’s zero_vectors theorem have no sorryAx dependency. There are no answer slots, bespoke definitions, or formal_proof attributes to audit. The original Wiley and AMS full-text links were inaccessible; their abstracts/metadata and the explicit primary follow-up statements supplied the cross-checks. The target file remains unchanged.
